skill.name: agent-communication-debugger
skill.description: Diagnoses A2A agent communication problems by checking agent status, message routing, transport connectivity, logs, and local configuration.
skill.summary: Debugs local A2A agent communication, routing, transport, and log issues.
skill.author: EGAdams

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown command examples for local troubleshooting. I confirmed one unmasked API key check in common_issues.md and several persistent nohup start commands; I also found restart guidance that can terminate local agent processes.

remediation.issue: Unmasked API key display in common_issues.md.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the raw OPENAI_API_KEY grep with a presence check or a masked command that never prints the secret value.
Require explicit user confirmation before running nohup commands and provide clear stop commands for every started process.

remediation.issue: Broad process termination commands in restart workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation, show matching processes first, and prefer targeted process IDs before using pkill patterns.

content.value_statement: Agent systems can fail through silent routing, transport, or configuration issues. This skill guides structured checks for processes, logs, environment, and message delivery.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether orchestrator, coder, tester, and WebSocket agent processes are running.
Inspects agent configuration files for names, topics, capabilities, and syntax issues.
Reviews logs for errors, routing decisions, connection failures, and message processing problems.
Tests message delivery with the included message test script.
Checks WebSocket and message board transport state for local agent communication.
Provides restart workflows for stuck local agents and transport services.
limitations: Assumes the project uses the documented a2a_communicating_agents and logs directories.
Requires local shell access and the required Python dependencies.
Identifies likely causes but does not automatically repair agent code.
Some restart steps can stop or start local processes and need review before use.

use_cases.title: Restore Silent Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Trace why an orchestrator or worker agent receives messages but does not respond.

use_cases.title: Verify Local Agent Services
use_cases.description: Check processes, local ports, logs, and transport state during a development environment incident.

use_cases.title: Run Communication Smoke Tests
use_cases.description: Send test messages and confirm that routing, responses, and storage paths behave as expected.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Agent Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent communication debugger to check which local agents are running and summarize any missing services.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Missing Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug why my message reached the orchestrator but no worker agent responded. Review logs, transport, and recent routing decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Wrong Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Find why code requests are routed to the wrong agent. Compare discovered agents, routing logs, and priority keyword mappings.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Full Transport Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a complete communication diagnostic across processes, configuration, logs, WebSocket transport, message board state, and test delivery results.

output_examples.input: The orchestrator is running, but the coder agent never replies.
output_examples.output: The report identifies whether the coder process is running, checks recent coder logs, verifies message delivery, and lists likely causes.

output_examples.input: Messages are reaching the orchestrator but routing to the wrong agent.
output_examples.output: The response compares routing logs with agent discovery data and recommends checking priority mappings, API key status, and ambiguous prompts.

output_examples.input: Run a full health check on the local agent system.
output_examples.output: The summary covers process status, configuration validity, recent errors, transport availability, and message test results.

best_practices: Run read-only status and log checks before restart commands.
Mask API key values and share only whether each variable exists.
Record the symptom, target agent, message text, and timestamp before diagnosis.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys or full environment files into chat.
Do not run broad restart commands before checking affected processes.
Do not assume routing is broken before verifying discovery and transport.

faq.question: What agent systems does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets local A2A agent systems with orchestrator, coder, tester, WebSocket, logs, and message board components.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: No external internet access is required for diagnostics. It may check local WebSocket services and local files.

faq.question: Can it fix routing problems automatically?
faq.answer: It guides diagnosis and points to likely routing changes. It does not automatically edit routing logic.

faq.question: Will it expose API keys?
faq.answer: The main workflow masks environment values, but users should avoid commands that print raw keys.

faq.question: Can it start or stop agents?
faq.answer: It includes restart commands for local agents. Review them before running because they affect local processes.

faq.question: Which tools does it use?
faq.answer: The skill uses Bash, Read, Grep, and Glob to inspect local processes, files, logs, and transport state.
